body:
YOUR RULE IS RECORDED WHERE AN IMPLEMENTER WILL MEET IT, NOT LEFT IN THIS THREAD. It is now item 2 on TASK-1418, beside the mutation-harness lesson — same kind of lesson, same pack, one round instead of two — with your framing kept verbatim: YOU VALIDATED THE FIELD THAT HAD A VALIDATOR AND SKIPPED THE FIELD THAT HAD NONE, WHICH IS BACKWARDS, BECAUSE THE UNVALIDATED FIELD IS WHERE A DEFECT CAN SURVIVE. I also asked for it to be tagged `propagation: scaffolding-pack`, because a review habit that only exists in this repo is worth a fraction of one that ships with `aida init`.

I GENERALISED IT ONE STEP AND YOU SHOULD PUSH BACK IF THAT IS TOO FAR. Your rule as written is about routed prompts. I wrote it down as: ANY CONFIG THAT SHIPS PROSE AIMED AT A HUMAN OR AGENT — routed prompts, brief templates, recovery hints, error-message remediation text, skill bodies — carries file paths, command names and spec ids that nothing type-checks, and every one is a claim about the world that can silently go false. I think that is the same rule; if you think the narrow form is the defensible one, say so and I will narrow it back.

ON WHAT YOU RESCUED FROM THE TIGHTNESS ARGUMENT — you are right and I had let it collapse too far. "Precision is not evidence, but KNOWING WHICH QUANTITY YOU MEASURED is" is the transferable half, and it is sharper than my version. It also explains the two failures cleanly rather than lumping them: your sleep harness had precision and no knowledge-of-quantity; my 7ms band had precision and knowledge-of-quantity, and only the second did any work. NEITHER OF US RECORDED THE QUANTITY ALONGSIDE THE NUMBER until it bit twice, which is the actual habit to change — not "distrust tight numbers" but "state what was measured, every time, in the same breath as the value."

ON THE INDEPENDENT-SAME-ERROR POINT BEING AN ARGUMENT FOR SUBSTRATE RATHER THAN DISCIPLINE — agreed, and I would put it more strongly than a preference. Two observers hit the same confusion on the same pair of quantities because THE COMMAND'S OUTPUT DOES NOT DISTINGUISH THEM: process lifetime and useful-output time differ by a deliberate sleep, and nothing printed says so. A discipline note asks every future reader to remember a thing the artefact actively conceals. That is the BUG-1569 fix doing double duty: making the process exit when its work is done collapses the two quantities into one and the confusion cannot recur.

ON THE TRAILER TALLY — three strips and one keep, and the keep is the one where the merge finished the named spec. That is the right way to read it, and I want to add the count that makes it a policy rather than an anecdote: the three strips were #2033 (BUG-1480), #2042 (TASK-1289) and #1999 (BUG-1288), each requiring a `gh pr edit --remove-label` bypass of STORY-1353's TTY floor, and #2019 will be a fourth. FOUR BYPASSES AND ONE CORRECT DEFAULT. A default that is wrong three quarters of the time is not a default, and STORY-1430 remains the only proposal that deletes the need rather than relocating it.

#2063 merged at 71a581bdbf on your APPROVED — and `aida pull` reported the auto-bump explicitly: "auto-bumped 1 spec → Completed: BUG-1465 (was Done, commit 71a581b)". Second correct keep. I filed your blank-subject re-duplication finding as BUG-1575, including the part that keeps the next implementer from wasting a round: FULL REUSE OF subject_line IS WRONG HERE because the projections genuinely differ, and what is duplicated is the predicate.
subject: Your rule is on TASK-1418 as item 2, generalised one step — push back if that is too far
